findings.title: Server's `build_profiles` breaks once the two new fields are required; no task updates it
findings.description:
Task 2.1 (lines 55-61) makes `leadership_weight` and `momentum_weight` required. Task 2.2 (lines 63-71) only updates call sites under `tests/`, and its catch-all at line 70 also searches only `tests/`. But `build_profiles()` builds `BehavioralProfile(...)` with only the six current fields. After Task 2.1 it raises `TypeError` for every profile in the config. This breaks:
- server startup at `src/migratory_server/server.py:71`
- `tests/test_simulation.py::TestBuildProfiles::test_single_profile` and `test_multiple_profiles` (lines 27-42)
- `tests/test_server.py::test_server_runs_with_profiles_config` (config with `ProfileConfig` at lines 202-203, test at line 278)

So the check at line 71 fails, and the commit at Task 2.3 lands on a red suite. Task 2.2 needs a step to pass `leadership_weight=0.0, momentum_weight=0.0` in `build_profiles`. An alternative is to add defaulted fields to `ProfileConfig` (`src/migratory_server/config.py:51-60`) and parse them in `_validate_profile`. The slice only needs the first option.

findings.title: `EntityManager.spawn_population` merges arrays by hand and will leave `leadership` the wrong length
findings.description:
Task 1.1 (lines 31-38) updates `create`, `add_agent` and `remove_agent`. Task 1.2 (line 45) says the other callers "use `AgentState.create()` so they should work without changes". That's not true here. `spawn_population` builds a batch with `create()`, then concatenates `positions`, `velocities`, `accelerations` and `profile_indices` straight into `self._state`, but not `leadership`. After any population spawn, `state.leadership.shape != (N,)`. That breaks the slice invariant (slice lines 212-213). It causes:
- `remove_entity` → `remove_agent` → `np.delete(self.leadership, index)` raises `IndexError` for spawned indices (`entities.py:161`)
- a later `add_agent` puts leadership values at the wrong indices
- `LeadershipForce` would index `state.leadership[neighbors]` out of range in any server run

Current tests don't remove an entity after `spawn_population`, so the suite stays green and the bug stays hidden. Task 1.1 should add the `leadership` concatenation at `entities.py:145`, and Task 1.2 should add a test in `tests/test_entities.py` that spawns a population and checks `state.leadership.shape`.

findings.title: Test count claim is wrong ("80 tests")
findings.description: The frontmatter `projectState` (line 7) and Task 6.1 (line 173, "existing 80 + new herding tests") say there are 80 tests. `tests/` defines 229 `def test_` functions across 14 files, for example `test_config.py` 51, `test_entities.py` 28, `test_server.py` 24, `test_server_tick.py` 22. A junior checking against "80" will either think tests are missing or ignore the count. The number also hides that the server tests, which the plan never mentions, are in scope for regressions.

findings.title: `LeadershipForce` steps don't say how `neighbor_lists` is indexed
findings.description: `tick()` builds `neighbor_lists` in the order of `eval_indices`, so `neighbor_lists[k]` belongs to `active_indices[k]`, not to agent `k`. The flocking forces handle this with `enumerate(eval_indices)` (`src/migratory/engine/flocking.py:30-31`). Task 4.1 (lines 113-121) says "for each active agent … filter self from neighbors" but never states this mapping. A junior who writes `neighbor_lists[agent_idx]` gets wrong neighbors or an `IndexError` whenever `active_indices` is a subset. The active-indices test in 4.2 (line 131) only catches this if its `neighbor_lists` has length `len(active_indices)`, not N, and the plan doesn't say so. Add both: a step saying "use `neighbor_lists[list_idx]` with `enumerate(eval_indices)`, as in flocking.py", and a requirement that the isolation test passes subset-length lists.

findings.title: Vectorization requirement isn't traced to any step
findings.description: Slice line 395 says: "Both forces are vectorized within each agent's neighborhood — no nested Python loops." Task 4.1 line 118 writes the weighted heading as `sum(velocity[i] * leadership[i]) / sum(leadership)`, which reads like a per-neighbor loop. No step requires the vectorized form, e.g. `w = state.leadership[nbrs]; (state.velocities[nbrs] * w[:, None]).sum(0) / w.sum()`, and nothing checks it. Task 3.1 should also say MomentumForce works on whole arrays.

findings.title: Leadership "known case" test checks direction only, not the actual output
findings.description: The slice criterion at line 384 says "Each force produces the correct output for hand-constructed inputs." Task 4.2 line 126 only checks that the force "biases toward agent 1's heading". The exact value is easy to compute: weighted = (0.1·[0,1] + 0.9·[1,0]) / 1.0 = [0.9, 0.1]. Minus agent 2's velocity [0,0], times `leadership_weight` 1.0, gives [0.9, 0.1]. A wrong version, such as one that normalizes or forgets to divide by the weight sum, would still pass a direction check. The uniform-leadership test (line 127) could also assert exact equality with `AlignmentForce` output when `alignment_weight == leadership_weight`. That holds exactly, so "similar" is weaker than it needs to be.

findings.title: Commit steps are checkbox tasks, not plain `**Commit**:` lines
findings.description: Commits appear as numbered checkbox tasks with checkbox steps: 1.3 (48-49), 2.3 (73-74), 3.3 (103-104), 4.3 (134-135), 5.4 (164-165) and 6.3 (180-182). They should be plain `**Commit**: <message>` lines. They're placed at sensible points, apart from 2.3, which comes after a red suite (see the FAIL finding). Task 6.3 also commits "remaining changes" after 6.1 and 6.2, which change no files, so it will be an empty or failing commit. Either drop it or name what it commits, e.g. updating the task and slice `status` frontmatter.

findings.title: Task 5.1 has no real assertion and overlaps Task 5.2
findings.description: Task 5.1 only asserts that 10 ticks run "without error". Line 144 ("set some agents to high leadership … to confirm forces interact correctly") names no check. Task 5.2 already runs all five forces through `tick()` with leaders. Either merge 5.1 into 5.2, or give 5.1 a concrete assertion such as a finite, correctly shaped state after N ticks.

findings.title: Task 6.2 repeats protocol checks already done, and the check is weak
findings.description: `isinstance(..., BulkForce)` is already checked in 3.1, 3.2, 4.1 and 4.2. `BulkForce` is `runtime_checkable`, so `isinstance` only confirms a `__call__` exists, not its signature. Task 6.2 adds nothing and can be removed.

findings.title: Task 5.3's "statistically measurable" with "or" is weaker than the slice walkthrough
findings.description: Slice lines 474-476 expect lower heading variance and an eastward bias. Line 161 accepts either one. The slice's technical requirement (line 403-405) does allow any single metric, so this is acceptable. But a single seeded run is deterministic, not "statistical". Stating the exact metric, e.g. circular variance of unit headings, would make the test unambiguous. Task 5.2 also doesn't set the speed range for the "random velocities" or say how mean heading is computed (mean of unit vectors or mean velocity).

findings.title: `test_missing_new_field_raises_type_error` already exists in test_profile.py
findings.description: Task 2.2 line 65 says to "add test for missing new field raises TypeError". A test with that exact name already exists and omits four fields. A new test with the same name would silently replace it. Rename the new test, e.g. `test_missing_leadership_weight_raises_type_error`, and add asserts for the new fields to `test_construction_with_all_fields` (lines 22-29).

findings.title: No step creates the branch the frontmatter mentions
findings.description: `projectState` says "Branch to be created from main", but no task does it, so the commits in 1.3 onward would go straight to `main`. Add a first step that creates the branch.
